name: Fascia lata

bony_attachments.landmark: via iliotibial tract to Gerdy's tubercle

compartment_contents: all thigh muscles (subdivided by its 3 intermuscular septa)
function: Dense tubular deep fascia of the thigh; its lateral thickening (iliotibial tract) is the strongest fascial structure in the body, tensioned by gluteus maximus and tensor fasciae latae to stabilize the knee in stance.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Iliotibial (IT) tract/band
function: Lateral thickening of fascia lata; acts as a tension member stabilizing the hip and knee during single-leg stance/gait, and (per Stecco) as a myofascial force-transmission pathway linking gluteus maximus and TFL to the tibia.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior (lateral) intermuscular septum of the thigh
function: Separates the anterior (quadriceps, femoral n.) from the posterior (hamstring, sciatic n.) thigh compartment laterally.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Medial intermuscular septum of the thigh
function: Separates the anterior compartment from the medial (adductor, obturator n.) compartment.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior intermuscular septum of the thigh
function: Separates the medial (adductor) from the posterior (hamstring) compartment.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior osteofascial compartment of the thigh
function: Contains the hip flexors/knee extensors, all femoral-nerve innervated.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Medial (adductor) osteofascial compartment of the thigh
function: Contains the hip adductors, predominantly obturator-nerve innervated (adductor magnus's hamstring part is the documented exception, sciatic-innervated).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior (hamstring) osteofascial compartment of the thigh
function: Contains the hamstrings, sciatic-nerve innervated.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Crural (deep) fascia of the leg
function: Dense tubular deep fascia of the leg, thickened proximally (forms part of the pes anserinus attachment) and distally into the ankle retinacula; gives origin to superficial fibers of several leg muscles directly from its deep surface.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior intermuscular septum of the leg
function: Separates the anterior compartment from the lateral (fibular) compartment.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior intermuscular septum of the leg (transverse crural septum)
function: Separates the superficial from the deep posterior compartment.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Interosseous membrane (leg)
function: Fibrous sheet linking tibia and fibula; separates the anterior from the deep posterior compartment, transmits load from fibula to tibia, gives origin to deep muscle fibers (tibialis anterior, tibialis posterior, EHL, FHL).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior osteofascial compartment of the leg
function: Ankle/toe dorsiflexors, deep-fibular-nerve innervated. Tightly enclosed by unyielding fascia -- classic site of acute compartment syndrome after tibial fracture.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lateral osteofascial compartment of the leg
function: Ankle evertors, superficial-fibular-nerve innervated.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial posterior osteofascial compartment of the leg
function: Primary ankle plantarflexors.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deep posterior osteofascial compartment of the leg
function: Toe flexors + tibialis posterior, tibial-nerve innervated.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Flexor retinaculum (of the ankle, forms the tarsal tunnel)
function: Roofs the tarsal tunnel behind the medial malleolus; compression here (tarsal tunnel syndrome) affects the tibial nerve, analogous to carpal tunnel syndrome in the wrist.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Extensor retinaculum (superior + inferior, of the ankle)
function: Prevents bowstringing of the anterior compartment tendons during ankle dorsiflexion; analogous in function to the wrist's extensor retinaculum.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: (Superior + inferior) fibular (peroneal) retinaculum
function: Retains the fibularis tendons behind the lateral malleolus.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Plantar aponeurosis (fascia)
function: Thick central band of the plantar fascia supporting the medial longitudinal arch; the 'windlass mechanism' -- toe dorsiflexion tensions the aponeurosis and passively raises the arch during late stance/push-off. A classically overuse-injured structure (plantar fasciitis).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Fibrous flexor sheaths (toes, annular + cruciate pulleys)

bony_attachments.landmark: plantar surface of each phalanx and MTP/IP joint plates

function: Osteofibrous tunnels analogous to the hand's, keeping the long toe flexor tendons apposed to bone through the gait cycle.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- lower limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
